responses.concepts.observation: Increasing noise spreads the distribution of measurements out, creating deeper troughs and higher peaks in the sample. Increasing bias skews the distribution to the right for positive values. The sample data distribution's median is to the right of the true value.
responses.mission_1.bias_vs_variance: My prediction lines up with the statistics because the mean and median are close together and close to the truth, but the variance is high. Bias may not have high variance but is skewed from the true value.
responses.mission_1.more_samples: Taking more samples could help get a more accurate average, but it would not completely fix the noise. More samples would give more credence to the median/average value, but we may get the same proportion of outliers
responses.mission_1.prediction: A biased sensor would have a more normal distribution, but would have the median skewed left or right, with clustering at those points. responses.mission_1.robot_consequence: If the robot bases its movement on outliers, it may attempt to move past the 2m obstacle and collide with whatever or whoever is in its path.
responses.mission_2.comparison: I expected the larger windows to be smoother but to have a longer delay. However, window 3 had the smallest RMSE value of only 0.136, while window 7 was at 0.1468 and window 11 had 0.1564. The delay was surprisingly higher for window 3 at 1.25 seconds compared to 1.1 seconds for both larger windows. The moving average and median were very similar for a window of 3 and a weight of .25. The moving average had an RMSE of 0.136, while the median had 0.1366, and both had a delay of 1.25 seconds. I was correct that relying more on sensor A/increasing its weight would increase error, but delay stayed the same.
responses.mission_2.fusion_choice: I think weight 0.50 with a window of 3 is the most preferable. All three had the same response delay of 1.25 seconds. All 3 had the same delay, so it is not a factor in the decision. Weight 0.25 had an RMSE of 0.1366, weight 0.50 had 0.1265, and weight 0.75 had 0.1335.
responses.mission_2.prediction_draft: Increasing the weight to .5 may reduce delay. However, Sensor A also has more noise and outliers, so giving it more weight could increase the effect of inaccurate readings.
responses.mission_2.responsiveness: A larger window doesn't always mean a longer delay. Even though the difference is only 0.15 seconds, it could matter if a fast object suddenly appeared in the robot's line of sight. A slower response could mean the robot doesn't stop in time
